newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end technical bourse trade higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares end technical bourse trade higher.

text.p: German shares traded higher over the course of bourse trade on Thursday, but dealers said the market was driven predominantly by technical factors rather than by any new data moving the market.

The DAX index, which tracks bourse trade, moved in a range of only 15 points over the session and ended the day up 19 points, or 0.51 percent, at 3,749.27 points, while the June DAX future was up 45.5 points at 3,772.5 points.

Derivative products drove the market ahead of Friday's "triple-witching", which sees the expiry of DAX index options, DAX futures and stock options and traditionally brings volatility into the market.
"This market is more technical than fundamental at the moment ahead of the triple witching, and it's causing movements right across Europe, not just in Germany," said a Frankfurt trader.
Derivatives buying lifted Volkswagen AG in particular early on, with the share ending the floor session at 1,247 marks, up 27.2 marks, the dealer said.
Technical factors also drove airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG higher, rising 1.83 marks to 34.40 marks.
Shares in retailer Karstadt fell by 28.50 marks to 625.50 marks, after disappointing five month figures.
"There isn't really any news out there -- it's all derivatives-driven. There is a lot of progressive buying coming from the U.S., and demand exceeds supply in this market," the trader said.

Derivatives-led selling saw German bank shares take a pounding, with Deutsche Bank AG down 50 pfennigs at 98.25 marks, Dresdner Bank AG down five pfennigs at 60.90 marks and Commerzbank AG down 40 pfennigs at 48.35 marks.
